title: Barnes Emergency Help Points
summary: Emergency medical locations, urgent treatment centres, and hazard guidance for Barnes, Barnes Bridge, and Mortlake.
content: For immediate life-threatening emergencies, always dial 999 or 112 first. 1. Nearest 24-Hour A&E Hospitals: Charing Cross Hospital, Fulham Palace Road, Hammersmith, London W6 8RF (from Barnes Bridge station: ~25 min walk northeast across Barnes Bridge and along Castelnau / Fulham Palace Road, or bus 209 to Hammersmith Bridge then walk across). Chelsea and Westminster Hospital, 369 Fulham Road, London SW10 9NH. For designated Major Trauma care, the regional centre is St George's Hospital, Blackshaw Road, Tooting, London SW17 0QT. 2. Urgent Treatment Centres: Queen Mary's Hospital Minor Injuries Unit / Urgent Treatment Centre, Roehampton Lane, Roehampton, London SW15 5PN (from Barnes station: ~15 min walk south along Rocks Lane and Roehampton Lane, or bus 72, 265, or 493). 3. Area Hazards: The tidal River Thames surrounds the Barnes peninsula; high risk of tidal inundation affects The Terrace, Lonsdale Road, Mortlake High Street, and Barnes Waterside during spring tides. Beverley Brook crosses south Barnes with additional surface and fluvial flood risk. 4. Supplies: Community pharmacies and supermarkets along Barnes High Street, Church Road, and Upper Richmond Road West (East Sheen / Mortlake) stock drinking water, first-aid items, and essential medicines during prolonged network disruptions. Note: addresses and opening hours may have changed — confirm on arrival where possible.
